explain.say: A speed camera has two jobs: measure how fast a car is going, and record evidence of which car it was. Fixed cameras sit by the roadside, and in the UK most are painted yellow.

explain.say: Many cameras bounce radar waves off the car. The reflected waves come back at a slightly changed frequency, the Doppler effect, and that change reveals the speed. Others use sensors in the road that time the car between two points.

explain.say: If the car is over the limit, the camera takes photographs. Evenly spaced lines painted on the road act as a check: in two photos taken a fixed time apart, the distance the car moved confirms its speed.

faq.a: They are usually placed where crashes have happened or speeding is especially dangerous, such as near schools and on accident blackspots.
asks: Why is there a speed camera here?

faq.q: How does a radar speed camera work?
faq.a: It sends out radio waves that bounce off the moving car. The reflected waves come back with a slightly changed frequency, the Doppler effect, and the size of the change gives the speed.

faq.q: How does a camera know the speed limit?
faq.a: Each camera is set up with the speed limit for its stretch of road and only triggers above it.
asks: Do speed cameras know the limit?

faq.q: Why are there white lines painted on the road near speed cameras?
faq.a: The lines are evenly spaced. Two photos taken a set time apart show how far the car moved across them, a second check of its speed.
asks: What are the marks on the road by a speed camera?

faq.q: How do average speed cameras work?
faq.a: Cameras read your number plate at the start and end of a stretch. Dividing the distance by the time between the readings gives your average speed.
asks: Can you slow down for an average speed camera?

facts: Speed is distance divided by time, which is how average speed cameras work.
Radar speed cameras and speed guns use the Doppler effect.
In the UK most fixed speed cameras are painted yellow so drivers can see them.

quiz.say: An average speed camera sees a car at two points 10 kilometres apart, 6 minutes apart. What was its average speed?
quiz.show: An average speed camera sees a car at two points 10 kilometres apart, 6 minutes apart. What was its average speed?
quiz.why: 10 kilometres in 6 minutes, a tenth of an hour, is 100 kilometres per hour.

wrong.1: That would mean 10 kilometres took 10 minutes.
wrong.2: That would mean 10 kilometres took a whole hour.
